discipline_framing: Semiotics, visual communication theory, and cultural analysis applied to decoding signs, aesthetics, and brand symbolism in trend intelligence
audience: Trend analysts, brand and design strategists, cultural researchers, and marketers who must decode what aesthetics like cottagecore or cyberpunk and brand symbols actually mean — and how meanings shift
sources: Saussure, Course in General Linguistics — signifier/signified, the structuralist foundation
Peirce's semiotic — icon/index/symbol triad and unlimited semiosis (via Chandler and Eco)
Barthes, Mythologies, 'Rhetoric of the Image', and The Fashion System — denotation, connotation, myth
Chandler, Semiotics: The Basics — the standard working introduction
Kress & Van Leeuwen, Reading Images: The Grammar of Visual Design — social-semiotic image analysis
Eco, A Theory of Semiotics, and Berger, Signs in Contemporary Culture for applied cultural analysis
Commercial semiotics practice literature (Semionaut lineage, cultural-code mapping in brand research) and aesthetic-taxonomy sources (Aesthetics Wiki documentation)
pitfalls: Unconstrained interpretation — reading any meaning into any sign without systematic method or contextual evidence
Treating connotation as fixed dictionary fact rather than culturally and historically variable
Analyzing signs in isolation from the syntagms, codes, and audiences that give them meaning
Confusing the analyst's decoding with the audience's actual reading (encoding/decoding mismatch)
Aesthetic labeling without analysis — using 'cottagecore' as a vibe tag rather than decoding its sign system
